findings.observation: Sheet 5 contains a block titled 'AUSTIN ENERGY STANDARD NOTES' (Block 7) with 5 numbered notes. The first 4 notes address: (1) tree pruning and easement clearing rights with Chapter 25-8 compliance, (2) easement/access provision obligations for electric facilities with Chapter 25-8 compliance, (3) owner responsibilities for erosion control, revegetation, tree protection, and initial tree work within 10 feet of overhead electrical facilities, and (4) owner responsibility for maintaining NESC, OSHA, and City clearances near overhead power lines. A 5th note regarding relocation costs at landowner's expense is also present. I compared these against the reference material in the General Site Plan Notes for COA document, which specifies 4 required notes.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires 4 standard Austin Energy notes covering tree pruning/easement rights, easement/access obligations, erosion control responsibilities, and NESC/OSHA clearance maintenance. The validation methodology requires approximately 90% semantic matching - notes don't need to be character-for-character identical but must preserve substantive meaning. All 4 required notes are present on Sheet 5 and semantically match the reference template. Note 1 preserves the tree pruning rights and Chapter 25-8 compliance language. Note 2 covers easement/access obligations with Chapter 25-8 compliance. Note 3 addresses erosion control, revegetation, tree protection, and the 10-foot clearance requirement. Note 4 covers NESC, OSHA, and clearance maintenance obligations. The 5th note about relocation costs is an additional note beyond the required 4, not a modification of the required notes, so its presence does not constitute a deficiency.
findings.explanation: All 4 required Austin Energy standard notes are present on Sheet 5 and semantically match the template requirements at approximately 90%+ threshold.

findings.observation: I reviewed the site zoning information from facts.md and the cover sheet. The site consists of three tracts with the following zoning: Tract 1 (3.44 ac) is zoned CS-V-DB90 (Commercial Services, Vertical Mixed Use, Density Bonus 90), Tract 2 (0.16 ac) is zoned CS-V-CO (Commercial Services, Vertical Mixed Use, Conditional Overlay), and Tract 3 (1.61 ac) is zoned CS-V-CO. None of the tracts are zoned CBD (Central Business District) or DMU (Downtown Mixed Use). The Consolidated Site Plan Application (Section 10) confirms 'Requires a Green Building Program Rating? [ ] Yes (x) No', with 'No' checked. I searched the supplementary documents and found no Letter of Intent.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item AEGB-02 has a condition of 'If zoned CBD or DMU'. The site is not zoned CBD or DMU - it is zoned CS-V (Commercial Services - Vertical Mixed Use) with DB90 and CO overlays. According to the grouping overview, the Letter of Intent is required at the site plan stage for projects zoned CBD or DMU under Downtown Design. Since this site does not meet the CBD or DMU zoning condition, the Letter of Intent requirement does not apply. The application form further confirms this by indicating 'No' for the Green Building Program Rating requirement. Therefore, this checklist item is not applicable to this site plan.
findings.explanation: Site is zoned CS-V-DB90 and CS-V-CO, not CBD or DMU. The condition for requiring a Green Building Letter of Intent is not met.

summary: All 4 checklist items evaluated: 3 items pass (AE-01 standard notes, AE-02 existing electric facilities, AE-03 proposed electric facilities), 1 item not-applicable (AEGB-02 Green Building Letter of Intent due to CS-V zoning, not CBD/DMU).
